title: Functoriality of strict henselization schemes
statement: For schemes S,T, a morphism g:T to S and geometric points s:Spec Omega to S and t:Spec Omega to T over the same algebraically closed field, suppose s=t composed with g. There exists f:T_(t) to S_(s) whose composite with the structural map to S equals the structural map to T followed by g. The schemes and structural maps are those of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] and [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map].

source.place: Tag 03Q9, affine pointed-neighbourhood inverse limit; functoriality as in Algebra Tag 04GU

proof.text: Reindex the canonical spectrum limit cone across the double-opposite equivalence. Postcompose by the inverse Gamma-Spec unit, whose components are isomorphisms on the affine neighbourhoods. The leg formula is Spec.map of GammaSpecIso.inv. Its composite with the neighbourhood map is the named structural map.

The representative functor into all pointed etale neighbourhoods is initial by strictHenselization_properties. Use Functor.Initial.extendCone and isLimitExtendConeEquiv to extend the preceding cone and its limit property. The arrow homToLift is over the base, so every extended leg still composes to the structural map.

Pull back each neighbourhood along g, with point given by pullback.lift of its point and t, using hst. The pullback maps give a functor on pointed categories of elements; prove its naturality by the two projections. Compose the extended t-cone legs at these pullbacks with pullback.fst, and prove cone naturality from pullback.lift_fst.

Lift the resulting cone through the extended limit at s. Choose one pointed neighbourhood using cofiltered nonemptiness. The limit fac equation, the structural leg formula, pullback.condition and the t-structural leg formula give f composed with rho_s = rho_t composed with g.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_strictHenselizationSchemeMap
    {S T : Scheme.{u}} {g : T ⟶ S}
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    {s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S} {t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T}
    (hst : s = t ≫ g) :
    ∃ f : strictHenselizationScheme t ⟶ strictHenselizationScheme s,
      f ≫ strictHenselizationStructuralMap s =
        strictHenselizationStructuralMap t ≫ g
